docs.title: stacpkg
docs.text:
Copy assets from an existing STAC selection, check the destination, and keep the new hrefs, source locations, and file facts in STAC GeoParquet.

A package holds Item metadata and an asset lock. Asset bytes stay outside it unless included with build --include-assets. OCI distribution is optional. See the package format for file roles.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Relocate assets: copy a selection to another location.
  • Create and share a package: keep existing locations or include files for offline use.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
• CLI: commands, options, and defaults.
  • Items: STAC GeoParquet and embedded Collections.
  • Asset lock: locations, checksums, and validation results.

See Architecture for the package and transfer design.

docs.title: Architecture and scope
docs.text: stacpkg starts with published STAC data. Take a fixed selection, move it, and check that its metadata and asset contents still describe the same dataset.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• Move data close to edge workloads without rebuilding the source catalog.
  • Prepare repeatable inputs for secure or isolated environments.
  • Stage workshop data once so participants can use a prepared copy.
  • Detect changed or incomplete assets against a trusted snapshot.
  • Support local files and object storage without requiring a registry.
  • Transfer package files through OCI when a registry is useful.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text:
• Package data and table pipelines: package files, STAC GeoParquet, Collection metadata, and Arrow IPC.
  • Relocation and validation: source locations, copy checks, checksums, and validation results.
  • Package distribution: OCI transport, package contents, and registry authentication.

docs.title: ADR-001: Package data and table pipelines
Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use STAC GeoParquet for saved Item metadata and Arrow IPC between table commands. The CLI calls the same Python operations that notebooks use. Input adapters read selected Items.

A local package is a directory. The .pkg suffix is a name convention.

Path Role When present items.parquet Selected STAC Items and embedded Collection documents. Required. assets.lock.parquet Asset locations and file facts used for checks. Required in built and relocated packages. assets/ Copied asset bytes with relative hrefs in the Items table. With build --include-assets. Other files or directories Context such as a license or handover notes. With build --includes PATH.

By default, assets remain at the hrefs recorded in the tables. relocate copies them to its separate --target location. For an offline handover, include asset bytes with build --include-assets.

Preserve Item property and extension fields, GeoParquet metadata, and complete Collection documents. Collections retain the source dataset description and extent; a selection does not recalculate them.

assets.lock.parquet has one row per selected Item asset location, identified by item_id and asset_key. Store structured locations and nullable file facts. Item IDs must be unique across the selection. The lock supplies checked file facts and copied locations for projection into Item assets. Keep credentials and check results outside the lock. The Asset Lock reference defines its fields.

Validation results go to stdout as JSON Lines.

Included assets use relative file paths. Their size and checksum describe the included copy. Original locations remain as alternates in Item metadata.

Adapters and Item transforms process Arrow batches. Operations that need the whole selection, such as copy planning and package validation, use tables. Update the output schema before writing fields added by a transform. JSON readers keep fields from all Items in a batch. Once an NDJSON stream has its schema, reject new fields or changed types rather than discard them.

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: STAC clients can read the metadata directly. Arrow retains field types and schema metadata between operations. Fixed filenames make a package usable on local storage without a registry or a separate package manifest.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Item assets.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use obstore for metadata queries and streaming transfers. Resolve relative hrefs from an explicit base, then an Item self link, then the input document. Packages with included assets keep source self URLs as via links, so their relative paths use the local Items document when the package moves. Permit named source alternates and runtime credentials, including S3 access when the primary HTTPS route is unsuitable. Saved hrefs must not contain credentials or temporary signed grants. Check Item and Collection assets, alternates, links, and endpoints.

Plan selected assets and target paths before copying. Reject duplicate identities and destination collisions. Bound copy buffers and worker counts. Write the completed package only after all required transfers pass. Failed runs can leave destination objects. Apply these rules to both relocation and asset inclusion. Build into a new directory, reject conflicting included paths, and publish the package only after all files are ready.

Hash the source stream and compare an independent full-object destination checksum, or read the destination back. Set target hrefs and retain original alternates after verification.

Store checksums as lowercase hexadecimal Multihash. Calculate SHA-256 for new facts. Keep ETags separate. Compare source STAC checksums with calculated or comparable provider checksums before replacing declarations. Offline derivation records locations and declared sizes, without importing checksums.

Checksum methods are metadata, use-etag, calculate-if-needed, and calculate-always. Table operations default to metadata; package validation defaults to calculate-if-needed. Package relocation always hashes the source stream and checks the destination. See the Asset Lock reference for provider rules.

Validation checks the full required asset set and Item/lock agreement. Compare expected values before saving observations. Check both declarations when Item and lock checksums use different algorithms. A matching checksum permits changed filesystem validators; report those changes separately and still check expected size.

Emit asset results and a summary as JSON Lines. Save checked facts atomically only after complete success. Preserve the prior lock on failure or metadata changes during validation. A first checksum observation is a baseline.

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: These checks support copies used for edge workloads, repeatable runs, and isolated environments. File facts stay portable, while check results describe a particular observation. Checksums need a trusted baseline to detect tampering.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Keep local packages usable without OCI. Use oras-py for optional registry push and pull. Artifacts carry typed layers for the Items table, asset lock, optional file archives, and included assets. Descriptors record digests, sizes, media types, and safe relative paths. Reject paths that escape the output directory. Check each downloaded layer against its digest and size before using it. Stage the package and publish the output directory after all required files pass. Reject duplicate package paths.

Both tables are required in the OCI artifact. Included asset bytes travel with it; externally referenced assets stay at their recorded locations. Preserve every included file during transport. The two required table paths are reserved for package tables. Push uploads package files. Pull checks package layers. Use validate to check the assets after delivery.

Use an empty OCI config. Package information belongs in the files and layer descriptors. Runtime configuration supplies registry credentials. Expose the oras authentication backend, defaulting to token; basic, plain HTTP, and TLS certificate checks are independent choices.

docs.title: Reason
docs.text:
Local and registry delivery serve different environments. OCI provides content digests for the delivered package files.

Reference: OCI distribution.

docs.title: Offline handover
docs.text: Use a local selection with its source files under openaerialmap-local-assets/. This example moves that source directory after building the package.

docs.title: Include the assets
docs.text:
stacpkg items from-parquet openaerialmap.items.parquet \
  | stacpkg build source.pkg --include-assets --include-metadata-assets

docs.title: Copy the package and make the original source unavailable
docs.text:
cp -R source.pkg delivered.pkg

mv openaerialmap-local-assets source-unavailable

docs.title: Check the delivered files
docs.text:
stacpkg validate delivered.pkg > validation.jsonl

tail -n 1 validation.jsonl

stacpkg inspect delivered.pkg --format markdown

docs.title: S3 and OCI handover
docs.text: Start with openaerialmap.items.parquet and accessible source assets. Prepare two S3 buckets and an OCI registry with runtime credentials. This example uses local endpoints at ports 19000, 19010, and 15000. Use new package directories and destination prefixes for each run.

docs.title: Copy to provider storage
docs.text:
stacpkg items from-parquet openaerialmap.items.parquet \
  | stacpkg relocate provider.pkg \
      --target s3://s3store1/selection/ \
      --target-endpoint-url http://127.0.0.1:19000 \
      --include-metadata-assets

docs.title: Deliver to recipient storage
docs.text:
The provider package records the source endpoint and verified file facts.

stacpkg items from-parquet provider.pkg/items.parquet \
  | stacpkg relocate recipient.pkg \
      --target s3://s3store2/selection/ \
      --target-endpoint-url http://127.0.0.1:19010 \
      --include-metadata-assets

stacpkg validate recipient.pkg

docs.title: Send metadata through OCI
docs.text:
The metadata points to assets in recipient storage. Registry credentials must be available through the runtime authentication setup.

stacpkg push recipient.pkg localhost:15000/stacpkg/selection:demo \
  --auth-backend basic --plain-http

stacpkg pull localhost:15000/stacpkg/selection:demo \
  --output-dir received.pkg --auth-backend basic --plain-http

stacpkg validate received.pkg

docs.title: Relocate selected assets
docs.text: Start with a local STAC GeoParquet selection. The test uses the downloaded OpenAerialMap thumbnails.

docs.title: Copy the selected thumbnails
docs.text:
The command checks destination contents, then writes the package with new primary hrefs and original alternates.

stacpkg items from-parquet openaerialmap.items.parquet \
  | stacpkg relocate verified.pkg --target copied-assets/ --asset-keys thumbnail

docs.title: Check the package again
docs.text:
Validation prints asset results and a summary. It saves the checked lock only after every asset passes.

stacpkg validate verified.pkg > validation.jsonl

tail -n 1 validation.jsonl

stacpkg inspect verified.pkg --format markdown

docs.title: Asset lock
docs.text: assets.lock.parquet records asset locations and object facts. One row names one STAC Item asset location and the facts available to check or move it later. The file does not contain asset bytes or saved validation results.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
The schema version is v1. item_id and asset_key are required. Other columns can be empty when a fact is unknown.

Column Arrow type Required Meaning item_id string Yes STAC Item id. asset_key string Yes STAC Asset key inside that item. store_type string No Obstore storage type name: file, s3, gs, az, http, or https. store_container string No Store container such as an S3 bucket, GCS bucket, Azure container, or HTTP origin. store_endpoint_url string No Optional object-store endpoint URL, such as https://s3.amazonaws.com or a MinIO endpoint, used when the bucket name alone is ambiguous. key string No Object key, path, or package-relative file path inside the store container. size_bytes int64 No Full object size in bytes, copied from STAC file:size, observed from object metadata, or observed after relocation. file_checksum string No Full-object checksum as lowercase hexadecimal Multihash. etag string No Backend object validator observed by metadata probing or relocation operations. last_modified string No Backend object last-modified timestamp observed by metadata probing or relocation operations, serialized as an ISO-8601 string when reported.

Validation results are not asset-lock columns. asset-lock validate computes valid and errors dynamically and prints JSON lines.

Assets whose key is metadata are skipped by default because these sidecar objects often repeat item or asset metadata already preserved in items.parquet. Use --include-metadata-assets to include them with the rest of the lock. An explicit --asset-keys metadata filter also includes them.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
Asset locations are structured instead of stored as a single href. The storage type names follow obstore (file, s3, gs, az, http, https), store_endpoint_url can record the S3-compatible endpoint that makes a bucket/key location unambiguous. Credentials stay outside the lock, including bucket-scoped S3 runtime variables such as STACPKG_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID_<BUCKET>.

When store_endpoint_url is empty, S3 operations fall back to runtime endpoint configuration from STACPKG_S3_ENDPOINT_<BUCKET>, STACPKG_S3_ENDPOINTS_JSON, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, or AWS_ENDPOINT.

docs.title: STAC mapping
docs.text:
items enrich writes File Info fields:

Asset lock STAC Asset field size_bytes file:size file_checksum file:checksum

Enrichment removes a source checksum when the lock has no checksum fact. Lock creation checks comparable source checksum declarations before returning observed facts. Asset inclusion checks declarations while copying, including when initial metadata queries are disabled.

When items enrich --alternate-key is used, reconstructed hrefs are written through the STAC Alternate Assets extension. If alternate hrefs are a mapped view of existing lock locations, create that mapped lock first with asset-lock relocate --dry-run, then pass it to items enrich.

Field definitions: Alternate Assets and File Info.

docs.title: Checksum methods
docs.text:
build, asset-lock derive, asset-lock validate, and asset-lock relocate accept --checksum. Their default is metadata. Package validate defaults to calculate-if-needed. Package relocate always hashes the source stream and checks the destination independently.

Method Behavior metadata Use supported full-object provider checksum fields, if available. use-etag Also permit a single-part MD5 ETag. Reject weak and multipart ETags. calculate-if-needed Read bytes when no comparable provider checksum is available. calculate-always Read bytes even when metadata contains a checksum.

Calculation uses SHA-256 for a new checksum. Validation uses the expected algorithm when comparing an existing supported checksum. Supported algorithms are MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512. Provider field normalization requires FULL_OBJECT; composite and unsupported checksum fields are ignored. Use a calculation method to check bytes through S3.

--no-probe-metadata skips initial asset queries and does not fill file_checksum, regardless of the checksum option. With build --include-assets, the subsequent copy still reads bytes and saves checked facts. A dry-run destination plan can retain a checksum, but it is not evidence that the destination was checked.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
asset-lock validate reads lock rows and prints results. It does not rewrite a saved lock. validate PACKAGE also checks that Item metadata and lock rows name the same assets and locations. It replaces assets.lock.parquet atomically only after the full required selection passes.

Both paths compare known size, ETag, modification time, and checksum facts. A matching full-object checksum permits changed or unavailable ETag and modification-time values. These differences are reported in metadata_changes. Size is always compared when expected. Without a matching checksum, known expected storage facts must have comparable observations. A checksum mismatch or an unavailable comparable checksum fails the check. Failed package checks preserve the prior lock and expected checksum.

A package report has one JSON object per asset and a final summary. Asset results contain identity and location, valid, errors, method, expected_checksum, observed_checksum, comparison, and observed facts. Methods distinguish metadata, provider-ALGORITHM, etag-md5, and bytes-ALGORITHM. comparison=baseline means no prior checksum was available; comparison=match means the expected checksum matched. If the Item and lock use different algorithms, declaration_check records an additional comparison with the Item checksum. Both checks must pass. Failures use comparison=mismatch or comparison=unavailable. comparison=metadata means the check has no checksum comparison. A scope or input error emits a failed summary without claiming asset coverage.

The summary records checked, passed, failed, baseline, excluded, methods, checksum, lock_written, and the Items file digest. The metadata asset key is excluded unless present in the lock. Other missing or extra rows, duplicate identities, and Item/lock disagreements fail the package check. Package checks require Item ids to be unique across the selection.

Save a report only when needed:

stacpkg validate selection.pkg > validation.jsonl

An ETag is a storage validator. Checksum promotion requires a service that uses single-part MD5.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Package commands work with directories. Table commands use Arrow IPC on stdin and stdout. When stdout is a terminal, table output is a short text preview.

docs.title: Streams and files
docs.text:
Use from-parquet and to-parquet to enter or leave a table pipeline. The adapters and Item transforms process batches. Package planning and validation hold the selection in memory.

--asset-lock PATH takes an Arrow IPC file, FIFO, or process-substitution path. It does not take Parquet or -; stdin carries the Items stream.

stacpkg items from-parquet items.parquet \
  | stacpkg items enrich \
      --asset-lock <(stacpkg asset-lock from-parquet assets.lock.parquet) \
  | stacpkg items to-parquet enriched.parquet

docs.title: Source and checksum options
docs.text:
relocate, build, and asset-lock derive accept:

Option Default Use --source-base URI Source context or Item self link Resolve relative hrefs. A directory URI must end in /. --source-alternate KEY Primary href Use this alternate for every selected asset. Missing alternates fail.

An explicit base takes priority, followed by an Item self link, then the input document path. Use runtime credentials for private stores. Saved hrefs and endpoints must not contain credentials or temporary signed grants.

build, asset-lock derive, asset-lock validate, and asset-lock relocate accept --checksum METHOD, defaulting to metadata. Package validate defaults to calculate-if-needed. Package relocate always hashes and checks the copy.

Choose metadata, use-etag, calculate-if-needed, or calculate-always. See Asset lock for their behavior.

docs.title: Storage credentials
docs.text:
Source locations come from the Item assets, or from --source-alternate. --target sets the destination for copied assets. Each store uses its own runtime credentials. Local files use filesystem permissions.

For S3, the storage library reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and optional AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. Use per-bucket environment variables when the stores need different credentials:

Setting Example for source-bucket Access key STACPKG_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID_SOURCE_BUCKET Secret key STACPKG_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_SOURCE_BUCKET Session token, if needed STACPKG_S3_SESSION_TOKEN_SOURCE_BUCKET Region STACPKG_S3_REGION_SOURCE_BUCKET Service endpoint STACPKG_S3_ENDPOINT_SOURCE_BUCKET

Replace SOURCE_BUCKET with the bucket name in uppercase, with each group of punctuation replaced by an underscore. For target-bucket, use TARGET_BUCKET. These settings apply by bucket name, on either side of a copy. Set both the access key and secret key when using per-bucket keys.

An endpoint stored with an asset takes priority over runtime endpoint settings. --target-endpoint-url sets the target endpoint. Without a per-bucket endpoint, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL or AWS_ENDPOINT can set a shared endpoint for S3-compatible storage.

Relocation needs source read access and target read and write access. Credentials are not stored in the package or passed as CLI options.

docs.title: relocate OUTPUT_DIR --target URI
docs.text:
Read Items, copy selected assets to the target, and write a package after all copies pass. The output directory must not exist. A failed run can leave target objects. Local targets must be outside the package directory; use build --include-assets to put bytes inside it.

Option Default Use --target URI Required Local directory or object-store prefix. --target-endpoint-url URL Runtime settings Destination object-store endpoint. --asset-keys KEY All except metadata Repeat to select keys. Other assets leave the output selection. --include-metadata-assets Off Also copy the metadata asset key. --collection PATH Embedded documents Repeat to supply Collection JSON. --overwrite Off Permit replacement of destination objects.

Source options are listed above; transfer settings are below. The output is a JSON summary. Library method: stacpkg.workflows.relocate_package.

docs.title: validate PACKAGE
docs.text:
Check assets against Item and lock facts. Print JSON Lines results and a final summary. Save the lock atomically only after all required assets pass. Missing or extra rows, duplicate identities, conflicting facts, or changed assets fail the check. Failure returns a non-zero exit code and keeps the prior lock.

Options: --checksum METHOD (default calculate-if-needed) and --max-workers COUNT (default 4). The Asset lock reference defines report fields. Library method: stacpkg.workflows.validate_package. Consume its iterator to completion to save the lock.

docs.title: build OUTPUT_DIR
docs.text:
Read Items and write a package directory. Assets stay at their current locations unless included. The output directory must not exist. Build publishes it after the package is complete. Included files must have distinct names and must not replace the tables or copied assets.

Option Default Use --asset-lock PATH Derive from Items Reuse an Arrow IPC lock. --collection PATH Preserve embedded documents Repeat to supply Collection JSON objects or arrays. --includes PATH None Repeat to include files or directories. --include-assets Off Copy selected assets under assets/ and set relative hrefs. --include-metadata-assets Off Include the metadata asset key when deriving the lock. --item-ids ID All Repeat to select Items. --providers NAME All Repeat to select providers. --probe-metadata, --no-probe-metadata Probe Query storage when deriving the lock.

Source and checksum options are listed above. Disabling the probe does not skip checks made by --include-assets. Explicit Collection documents replace embedded ones. Library method: stacpkg.dataset.build_package.

docs.title: inspect PACKAGE
docs.text: Print file digests, Item and asset counts, and embedded Collection IDs. Use --format {yaml,json,markdown,md}; the default is yaml.

docs.title: push PACKAGE TARGET and pull SOURCE --output-dir PATH
docs.text:
Transfer package files through an OCI registry. Pull requires a new output directory and checks each layer digest and size before publishing the directory. External assets stay at their recorded locations. Run validate after pulling to check the assets.

Option Default Use --auth-backend BACKEND token oras authentication backend; use basic for HTTP Basic authentication. --plain-http Off Use HTTP instead of HTTPS. --insecure Off Disable TLS certificate checks.

Runtime authentication can use ORAS_USER, ORAS_PASS, or Docker authentication settings. Basic authentication does not require either transport flag. Library methods: stacpkg.oci.push_package and stacpkg.oci.pull_package. See ADR-003 for artifact files.

docs.title: Item tables
docs.text:
All commands below start with stacpkg items.

Command Input Output from-json [FILE] Item or ItemCollection JSON; stdin if omitted. Items Arrow stream. from-ndjson [FILE] One Item JSON per line; stdin if omitted. Items Arrow stream. from-parquet FILE Local STAC GeoParquet. Items Arrow stream. to-parquet FILE Items Arrow stream. STAC GeoParquet file.

The three readers accept repeatable --collections ID, --providers NAME, and --item-ids ID filters. Repeated values within a filter are alternatives; different filters must all match. JSON input accepts Items and ItemCollections. Relative hrefs use the input document path or an absolute Item self link.

NDJSON and Parquet readers accept --batch-size ROWS, default 64000. The first NDJSON batch fixes the Arrow schema. Later batches can omit fields; new fields or changed types cause an error. Use JSON input for varied fields. The writer accepts repeatable --collection PATH inputs and preserves Collection metadata already in the stream.

docs.title: Asset hrefs and file facts
docs.text:
These commands read and write Items Arrow streams.

Command Required options Behavior promote-alternate --alternate-key KEY Make an alternate the primary href. remove-alternate --alternate-key KEY Remove that alternate and keep the primary. add-alternate --asset-lock PATH --alternate-key KEY Add hrefs reconstructed from the lock. enrich --asset-lock PATH Write lock size and checksum facts as File Info fields.

promote-alternate, remove-alternate, and add-alternate also accept --key as an alias for --alternate-key.

Promotion accepts --mode {replace,switch}, default replace. In switch mode, the old primary becomes the selected alternate. Set its name with --switched-alternate-name NAME, default original. --drop-alternates removes the alternate map after replacement and cannot be used with switch.

add-alternate accepts --alternate-name NAME (alias --name), defaulting to the alternate key. enrich --alternate-key KEY also adds a reconstructed href there. Enrichment removes a source checksum if the lock has no checksum fact.

docs.title: Collection documents
docs.text: stacpkg collections extract FILE [--output PATH] reads embedded Collection documents and writes a JSON array sorted by ID. Output goes to stdout when --output is omitted. Stored asset hrefs are preserved. See Items for the metadata format.

docs.title: Asset-lock tables
docs.text:
All commands below start with stacpkg asset-lock.

Command Input Output derive Items Arrow stream. Asset-lock Arrow stream. from-parquet FILE Asset-lock Parquet. Asset-lock Arrow stream. to-parquet FILE Asset-lock Arrow stream. Asset-lock Parquet. validate Asset-lock Arrow stream. JSON Lines results. relocate Source asset-lock Arrow stream. Destination asset-lock Arrow stream.

from-parquet accepts --batch-size ROWS, default 64000.

docs.title: derive
docs.text:
Derive locations and query current file facts. Options:

  • --item-ids ID, --providers NAME, and --asset-keys KEY: repeat to filter.
  • --include-metadata-assets: include the metadata asset key; it is skipped by default.
  • --probe-metadata or --no-probe-metadata: probing is on by default.
  • --keep-going: retain rows after recoverable metadata errors.
  • --max-workers COUNT: default 4.

Source and checksum options are listed above. Offline derivation records locations and known size facts. An explicit --asset-keys metadata also includes metadata assets.

docs.title: validate
docs.text: Compare current assets with locked facts. Options: repeatable --item-ids ID and --asset-keys KEY, --checksum METHOD (default metadata), --max-workers (default 4), and --keep-going. Exit status is zero only when every emitted result is valid. This command does not rewrite a saved lock.

docs.title: relocate
docs.text:
Choose a reviewed destination lock with --destination-lock PATH (Parquet), or describe a destination with --store-type {file,s3,gs,az,http,https}. These choices are mutually exclusive.

Option Default Use --store-container VALUE None Bucket, container, or HTTP origin; required except for files. --store-endpoint-url URL Runtime settings Destination object-store endpoint. --key PREFIX Empty Destination prefix; required for files. --source-prefix URI All Only map locations at or below this prefix. --layout {item-asset,source-key} item-asset Use Item/asset names or keep source object key paths. --dry-run Off Write destination rows without copying bytes or checking target existence. --overwrite, --no-overwrite Overwrite Control replacement of destination objects. --keep-going Off Retain rows after recoverable copy errors.

Checksum options are listed above. Rows match by item_id and asset_key. A destination lock can describe an alternate access route.

docs.title: Transfer settings
docs.text:
Package relocate and asset-lock relocate accept:

Option Default Use --max-workers COUNT 4 Maximum copy tasks. --memory-limit-bytes SIZE 2GiB Reserved transfer buffer budget. --chunk-size-bytes SIZE 8MiB Streaming chunk size. --put-max-concurrency COUNT 1 Multipart puts per task.

Sizes accept bytes or units such as 128MiB.

docs.title: Items
docs.text: items.parquet records the selected STAC Items for a package. One row represents one STAC Item. Item assets, properties, and links stay with that row.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
The field list, required flags, and nested links and assets shapes are defined by the STAC GeoParquet specification schema table.

The spec maps core Item fields such as id, geometry, bbox, links, assets, stac_extensions, and collection to Parquet columns, and promotes STAC properties entries to top-level property columns.

docs.title: Collection metadata
docs.text:
Collection documents are stored under the stac-geoparquet Parquet key:

{
  "version": "1.1.0",
  "collections": {
    "<collection-id>": {
      "...": "complete STAC Collection object"
    }
  }
}

The map key must equal the Collection object's id. Extension fields are preserved. The stac-geoparquet.version value and the stac_geoparquet:version key remain consistent. Existing embedded Collections flow through Arrow streams, filtering, alternate-asset transformations, enrichment, and package builds unless explicit Collection documents replace them.

Package metadata uses stacpkg:schema-kind=items and stacpkg:schema-version=v1 to identify the table. Standard GeoParquet geo metadata is preserved.

The Python write_items_geoparquet and build_package functions accept collections=. The CLI accepts repeatable --collection PATH inputs.

Collection embedding checks document type, non-empty IDs, mapping keys, duplicate IDs, and whether supplied documents cover Item collection IDs. Complete Collection JSON is preserved in the Parquet metadata. Collection assets, links, and endpoints are checked for credentials and signed access grants before saving. Descriptions and extents stay as published.

docs.title: Collection extraction
docs.text: collections extract FILE [--output PATH] writes a JSON array sorted by ID. It reads the collections map or singular collection field. Generate a separate Collection file after pull when a consumer needs it. Extraction keeps asset hrefs as stored.

docs.title: Field handling
docs.text:
geometry is stored as WKB with GeoParquet metadata. bbox follows the GeoParquet bounding-box column shape. links are stored as link structs, and assets are stored as nested asset structs using the STAC Asset keys from the items.

GeoJSON conversion supports Point, LineString, Polygon, and their Multi forms with XY or XYZ coordinates. Positions within one geometry must use the same dimensions. Bounding boxes retain Z limits. Links keep request fields and extension fields. Missing values are null.

STAC properties fields become top-level columns. Datetime-like property values are converted to UTC timestamp values when they can be parsed; values that cannot be parsed stay as their original values. Property names that collide with top-level STAC GeoParquet fields are not emitted as separate property columns.

JSON readers keep fields from all Items in a batch. NDJSON rejects new fields or changed types after the stream schema is set.

docs.title: Relocation and file facts
docs.text:
relocate writes copied target hrefs as primary locations and retains original locations under alternate.original. Selected --asset-keys define the output asset set. Other Item fields and Collection schema metadata are preserved.

items enrich writes lock size_bytes as file:size and file_checksum as file:checksum. It removes a source checksum when the matching lock row has no checksum fact. See the Asset Lock reference for methods and validation rules.

A package with included asset bytes uses relative target hrefs under assets/. Package validation resolves them against the local items.parquet path, so the package can move between local directories. Source self URLs are retained as via links in packages with included assets. The Parquet reader uses the same document base when a package becomes input for another copy. An explicit --source-base takes priority.

docs.title: Create and share a STAC package
docs.text: Start with an existing STAC selection. To copy assets to a separate target, use Relocate assets.

docs.title: Keep existing asset locations
docs.text:
stacpkg items from-json selection.json \
  | stacpkg build selection.pkg --checksum calculate-always

Build writes the two tables in the package format. Choose a new package directory. Build makes it available after all files are ready. The example reads bytes to calculate checksums. The default method, metadata, uses storage metadata. --no-probe-metadata skips those initial queries.

docs.title: Include asset bytes
docs.text:
stacpkg items from-json selection.json \
  | stacpkg build offline.pkg --include-assets --include-metadata-assets

cp -R offline.pkg delivered.pkg
stacpkg validate delivered.pkg > validation.jsonl

Build copies Item assets under assets/, checks their contents, and writes relative target hrefs. --include-metadata-assets also copies the metadata asset key, which is skipped by default. Copying still checks bytes when initial metadata probing is disabled.

See Offline handover for a complete run and its output.

Validation prints asset results and a summary. It replaces the lock only after all required assets pass. Failure keeps the prior lock and returns a non-zero exit code. A first checksum observation establishes a baseline.

docs.title: Keep Collection metadata and context
docs.text:
Add --collection collection.json to build. Repeat it for several documents; each file can hold one Collection or an array. Complete documents and extension fields stay in the Parquet metadata. Add notes or a license with --includes PATH.

Extract Collection documents when a consumer needs JSON:

stacpkg collections extract selection.pkg/items.parquet --output collections.json

Extraction keeps stored hrefs and the source dataset description.

docs.title: Share through OCI
docs.text:
stacpkg push offline.pkg registry.example/eo/selection:demo
stacpkg pull registry.example/eo/selection:demo --output-dir restored.pkg
stacpkg validate restored.pkg

Pull checks layer digests and sizes. Its output directory must not exist. It transfers included files; external assets must remain accessible to the recipient. Registry credentials come from runtime settings. Use validate for asset checks after delivery, as shown above.

docs.title: Relocate assets
docs.text: Use a STAC client to select existing Items as JSON or STAC GeoParquet.

docs.title: Copy and check
docs.text:
stacpkg items from-json selection.json \
  | stacpkg relocate relocated.pkg --target copied-assets/ --asset-keys thumbnail
stacpkg validate relocated.pkg > validation.jsonl

The example copies only thumbnails. Repeat --asset-keys to select more keys, or omit it for all except metadata. Set --include-metadata-assets to include that key. Only explicitly selected asset keys remain when a key filter is used.

The source locations come from the Item asset hrefs. --target sets where the asset files are copied. relocated.pkg holds the new metadata and asset lock; it is separate from the copied files.

Relocation hashes each source stream with SHA-256, checks any declared source checksum, and checks the destination independently. It writes target hrefs, original alternates, sizes, and checksums after all copies pass.

See Relocate selected assets for a complete run and its output.

For a tutorial or workshop, copy the selection to prepared storage. Give participants the package and read access to the copied assets so they can use the prepared copy without access to the source.

The package directory must not exist. Destination objects are replaced only with --overwrite. A failed run can leave copied objects at the target. Use build --include-assets to put bytes inside the package.

Validation compares assets with the lock and Item facts. It prints JSON Lines and keeps the prior lock on failure. See the Asset lock reference for result fields and baseline checks.

docs.title: Private storage
docs.text:
Choose an S3 alternate when the primary HTTPS href is unsuitable:

stacpkg items from-parquet selection.items.parquet \
  | stacpkg relocate relocated.pkg \
      --source-alternate s3 \
      --target s3://destination/selection/

Every selected asset must have that alternate. Either side can be local or remote. Supply credentials only for stores that need them:

Copy Access needed Private S3 to local Read access to the source bucket. Local to private S3 Read and write access to the target bucket. Private S3 to private S3 Read access to the source; read and write access to the target. Local to local File permissions on both sides.

The target needs read access because relocation checks the copied contents. Credentials come from runtime settings and stay out of the package.

For one S3 account, set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and, when needed, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. The local side does not use these settings. For separate accounts, use the per-bucket settings.

An asset can record its S3 store_endpoint_url; --target-endpoint-url sets the destination endpoint. Endpoints select a storage service; credentials give access to it. Saved locations must not contain credentials or temporary signed grants.

docs.title: Source paths and transfer settings
docs.text:
Relative hrefs use an explicit --source-base, then an absolute Item self link, then the source JSON or Parquet path. For an Arrow stream without source context, set --source-base to a document URI or a directory URI ending in /.

The CLI reference lists worker, chunk, and buffer settings. Select the Items and asset keys for the copy before relocation.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
Use the same operations in a notebook:

from stacpkg.workflows import relocate_package, validate_package

relocate_package("selection.json", "relocated.pkg", target="copied-assets/")
results = list(validate_package("relocated.pkg"))
print(results[-1])
